newsitem.title: USA: GM Buick City plant to be idled from strike.
newsitem.headline: GM Buick City plant to be idled from strike.

text.p: General Motors Corp workers at the automaker's Buick City car plant in Flint, Mich., were told to not report to work Thursday because of a strike at a transmission plant that began at midnight Tuesday.
GM spokesman Tom Klipstine said about 2,700 people are affected by the suspension of production at Buick City. The plant makes Buick LaSabre and Pontiac Bonneville sedans.
About 2,800 workers from United Auto Worker Local 909 struck the Warren, Mich., engine component plant when contract talks failed to produce a new agreement.

Kliptsine said by Thursday afternoon, one or two additional plants could also be affected. One possible facility could be the Orion Township, Mich., car plant that produces the Oldsmobile Eighty Eight and Aurora, as well as Buick Riviera and Pontiac Bonneville.
Starting Thursday morning, GM plans to start issuing updates on how the strike is affecting its North American production, he said.
Klipstine said minivan production is not likely to be affected until next week.

The Warren plant supplies four-speed automatic transmissions for front-wheel-drive cars vehicles. It also makes suspension control arms and wheels. A lengthy strike could seriously disrupt GM's North American production, analysts have said.
